questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go on exchange in a country where I could practice my French while studying.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy. I did not feel like I had any information until I showed up physically at my Erasmus coordinators office. When I did his response was: "There you are! I've been waiting you", even though he hadn't ask me to come.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I quickly learned that sending my coordinators emails was like talking to a wall whereas showing up physically always helped a lot. When in the room the coordinators were actually very nice and helpfull.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I assume 1 is worst and 5 is best.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a very stressed and chaotic proces. I ended up finding a private student housing company but is was both expensive and bad so I unfortunately can't recommend it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you are unlucky your accommodation is small, far away from the city center and expensive. If you are lucky your accommodation is close to the city center and expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not easy. It was more or less impossible to make my own course plan with the time tables. The only option ended up being following the whole study program for the local students during the semester I was there.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received around 10 - 15 almost unreadable time tables with small coloured course schedules all in abbreviations I did not know. So I had to go to the university's web page to see the courses they had and then guess which abbreviations were which courses. The next problem was that the time tables changed on a weakly basis for all courses making it impossible to build my own study plan. The final problem was communicating the courses I ended up choosing to my course coordinator. I had to show up at his office the day before the courses started because I still hadn't been added to the courses despite my many emails.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help on person, at my coordinators office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As described it was a long and stressful experience but it ended up working out the day before the courses started.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Trust the proces.

This was what I was told by a student I talked to who had done the same exchange program before me and it ended up being the best advice I got. My experience with France is that nothing ever goes as planned but that everything always end up well in time anyways. As a metaphor you could say that the busses never follow their time tables but just as you are about to give up, an unknown bus always shows up and gets you to the destination in time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very dedicated teachers.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took bachelor level courses, following the mandatory curriculum with the local students that were in the fifth semester of their BA as well as me.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Almost scarily similar. Maybe there was slightly more passion in the teaching but I think that might also just be due to the differences in the Danish and French mentality and expressiveness.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Astrophysique, Physique des milieux continus, Physique quantique 1, Optique et électromagnétisme, and Méthodes mathématiques.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ones I took if you are on exchange in your 5th semester.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The costs of getting a french guarantor (mandatory for everyone renting accommodation in France).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I ended up spending much more money on social things like café's and restaurants than I had expected. I guess that could have been prevented in principle, but in practice that is very very difficult in a city like Paris.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not attend to any but there seemed to be many cool things.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A broad variety of sports and art classes and social events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't really use any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I don't think I know a city with more museums, monuments and nice restaurants than Paris. The opportunities seem endless and in France most museums are free for everyone under the age of 26.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some weeks but I think that was mostly due to the fact that I was a new place. I don't think the cultural adjustment by itself was a big thing.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Maybe just take some chances. Because they are most likely not going to interact if you don't take the initiative.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Something as small and silly as the different selection in the grocery stores. So as I said, the cultural differences weren't overwhelming.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture of eating out and eating late.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Trust the proces. Things often seem stressful and impossible but usually help will turn up when you expect it the least. Just keep calm and don't panic.

- Show up aphysically when you have important questions. The academic structures can be complicated and non-logical but the people in the system are nice and ready to help.

- Reach out to other students! Especially other exchange students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You might hear a couple of times that the administration at Sorbonne is difficult to work with but don't get it wrong: It is definitely worth it and I think I have learned a lot from it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing that everything is gonna work out if you work for it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me it was studying in French. My level was probably around B2 (some things a bit under, some a bit over) but my experience was that you learn quickly when you hear it every day. And understanding the teachers is a lot easier than understanding your fellow students!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
